title: Doctrine of Ultra Vires — Substantive and Procedural Review

content.overview: Ultra vires means beyond the powers. In administrative law it is the primary legality test: an administrative act, order or subordinate legislation that exceeds the jurisdiction conferred by the Constitution or the parent statute is void. The doctrine covers substantive ultra vires (excess of power, improper purpose, irrelevant considerations, unreasonableness) and procedural ultra vires (failure to follow mandatory procedure). Courts quash ultra vires action; they do not rewrite the enabling statute.
content.glance: Identify the enabling power, the act challenged, whether the defect is jurisdictional or intra-vires, whether procedure was mandatory, and the precise remedy (quash, declare void, remit).
content.study:
Core rule: every exercise of public power must stay within the four corners of the enabling law. An act outside those bounds is ultra vires and liable to be set aside.

Substantive ultra vires: The authority lacked power; or had power but used it for a purpose foreign to the statute; or rested the decision on legally irrelevant considerations; or reached a result so unreasonable that no reasonable authority could have reached it. Article 14 supplies an independent constitutional check against arbitrary state action.

Procedural ultra vires: Where the statute or rules prescribe a mandatory procedure (notice, hearing, consultation, publication, previous sanction), non-compliance vitiates the act. Directory procedures may not produce the same consequence; the label turns on the language and purpose of the requirement.

Delegated legislation: Subordinate rules, notifications and bye-laws are ultra vires if they exceed the parent Act, conflict with it, or fail mandatory procedural conditions for their making. Challenges often combine ultra vires with Articles 14 and 19 where rights are engaged.

Remedies: Typical relief is certiorari or a declaration of invalidity, sometimes mandamus to compel a lawful exercise of power. The court does not ordinarily substitute its own administrative preference; it restores legality.

Current-law framing: Ground the analysis in the specific Constitution or statute that creates the power. Do not treat the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 as the source of ultra vires doctrine; evidence provisions apply only when proof or authenticity of material is actually in issue.

sections.heading: Meaning and Scope of Ultra Vires
sections.body: Ultra vires literally means beyond the powers. In public law it asks whether the decision-maker had legal authority to do what was done. The starting point is always the enabling provision — constitutional article, statute, or rule — and the limits it imposes on purpose, procedure and result.

sections.heading: Substantive Ultra Vires
sections.body: Substantive ultra vires covers excess of jurisdiction, action for an improper or collateral purpose, reliance on irrelevant considerations or failure to take mandatory considerations into account, and irrationality under the applicable reasonableness standard. Article 14 independently condemns arbitrary state action even where formal jurisdiction exists.

sections.heading: Procedural Ultra Vires
sections.body: Where the enabling law requires notice, hearing, consultation, publication or other steps as a condition of valid exercise of power, failure to follow a mandatory procedure makes the act procedurally ultra vires. Whether a requirement is mandatory or directory depends on the statutory language and the purpose the procedure serves.

sections.heading: Ultra Vires and Delegated Legislation
sections.body: Rules, regulations, notifications and bye-laws must stay within the parent Act. They are ultra vires if they enlarge or contradict the statute, if essential legislative policy is not laid down, or if mandatory rule-making procedure is ignored. Judicial review of subordinate legislation remains available on these legality grounds.

sections.heading: Remedies and Limits of Review
sections.body: The ordinary remedy is to quash the ultra vires act or to declare it void. Mandamus may compel a lawful re-exercise of power. Courts supervise legality; they do not redecide pure administrative merits unless the statute confers appellate power or the decision is legally untenable.

provisions.title: Equality and non-arbitrariness as a constitutional review standard
High Court judicial review and writ jurisdiction
Supreme Court writ jurisdiction for fundamental rights
Supreme Court special leave jurisdiction where engaged

examples.title: Excess of jurisdiction
examples.body: A statute authorises an authority to suspend a licence for specified breaches. The authority cancels the licence permanently. The issue is whether cancellation exceeds the conferred power and is therefore ultra vires.

examples.title: Mandatory procedure skipped
examples.body: Rules require prior notice and an opportunity to show cause before an adverse order. The order is passed without either step. The issue is procedural ultra vires and whether the requirement is mandatory.

examples.title: Rule enlarging the parent Act
examples.body: A parent Act caps a penalty at a fixed maximum. A subordinate rule authorises a higher penalty. The issue is whether the rule is ultra vires the parent statute.

hypotheticals.question: An authority has formal jurisdiction under a statute but uses the power for a collateral purpose. Is the decision ultra vires?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, if the purpose is foreign to the enabling provision. Identify the statutory purpose, the purpose actually pursued, and the material on the record. Improper purpose is a classic head of substantive ultra vires even where formal jurisdiction exists.

hypotheticals.question: A challenger disagrees with the administrative outcome on policy grounds. Is that enough to establish ultra vires?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Ultra vires requires a legal defect — excess of power, wrong purpose, irrelevant considerations, mandatory procedure ignored, or irrationality under the applicable standard. Pure policy disagreement is not, by itself, ultra vires.

distinctions.title: Ultra vires vs lawful exercise of discretion
distinctions.left: Ultra vires: the act is outside the legal power or violates mandatory limits.
distinctions.right: Lawful discretion: the authority chooses among options within the statutory bounds.

rows.left: Was the power exceeded or misused in law?
rows.right: Was the choice among lawful options rationally made?

rows.left: Act void or quashed as beyond power.
rows.right: Act stands unless a separate legality defect is shown.

distinctions.title: Ultra vires vs natural justice
distinctions.left: Ultra vires focuses on jurisdiction, purpose, considerations and mandatory statutory procedure.
distinctions.right: Natural justice focuses on fair hearing and impartiality, including common-law and Article 14 standards.

rows.left: Often the enabling statute or jurisdictional limits.
rows.right: Fairness principles, sometimes implied by statute or Constitution.

rows.left: Mandatory hearing clauses are also procedural ultra vires if ignored.
rows.right: Bias and fair-hearing claims may succeed even without a specific statutory clause.

misconceptions.trap: Any error of law or fact by the authority is automatically ultra vires.
misconceptions.correction: Ultra vires requires excess of power, improper purpose, irrelevant considerations, mandatory procedure failure, or irrationality under the governing standard — not every error.

misconceptions.trap: Wide statutory language makes ultra vires review impossible.
misconceptions.correction: Even wide powers must be used for the statutory purpose and without arbitrariness; formal breadth does not confer immunity.

misconceptions.trap: BSA provisions define when an administrative act is ultra vires.
misconceptions.correction: Ultra vires is a public-law legality doctrine grounded in the enabling statute and the Constitution; evidence law applies only to proof questions.

cases.name: Tata Cellular v Union of India
cases.facts: The case concerned judicial review of administrative decision-making in the context of government contracts and discretionary power.
cases.issue: What is the scope of judicial review over the exercise of administrative power?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court articulated limits on judicial review of administrative action, emphasising examination of the decision-making process for legality and rationality rather than substitution of commercial judgment.
cases.holding: The Court applied those review standards to the administrative decision under challenge.
cases.relevance: Leading authority on the scope and limits of judicial review, including ultra vires and rationality analysis.

cases.name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Maharaja Dharmander Prasad Singh
cases.facts: The case concerned the exercise of governmental power and the standards applicable to administrative action.
cases.issue: How should courts approach challenges to the exercise of administrative or governmental power?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court examined the legal limits on the exercise of the power and the appropriate intensity of judicial review on the facts before it.
cases.holding: The Court disposed of the appeal by applying the governing legal standards to the administrative action under challenge.
cases.relevance: Authority already present in the topic file on review of administrative power; case-law verification remains a separate gate.

cases.name: State of Tamil Nadu v P. Krishnamurthy
cases.facts: The case concerned challenges to subordinate legislation and the scope of judicial review over rule-making.
cases.issue: What grounds are available to challenge the validity of subordinate legislation?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The Court restated the established grounds on which subordinate legislation may be reviewed, including ultra vires and related legality defects.
cases.holding: The Court applied those grounds to the measure under challenge.
cases.relevance: Useful for ultra vires challenges to delegated legislation; verification remains a separate gate.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should an ultra vires challenge be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the enabling provision and the act challenged. II. Classify the alleged defect (excess of power, improper purpose, irrelevant considerations, mandatory procedure, irrationality). III. Distinguish substantive from procedural ultra vires and mandatory from directory requirements. IV. Apply Article 14 where arbitrariness is pleaded. V. Seek precise relief (quash, declare void, remit) without pure merits substitution.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the doctrine of ultra vires in Indian administrative law. Distinguish substantive and procedural ultra vires.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Introduce ultra vires as the primary legality test. Define substantive ultra vires (jurisdiction, purpose, considerations, reasonableness/Article 14). Define procedural ultra vires (mandatory statutory procedure). Note delegated-legislation challenges. Conclude with remedies (quash/declare) and the limit that courts do not redecide pure merits.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Discuss the doctrine of ultra vires as a tool of judicial control over administrative action and subordinate legislation. Illustrate with the heads of review and appropriate remedies.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Concept and constitutional setting (Articles 14, 226, 32/136). II. Substantive ultra vires heads. III. Procedural ultra vires and mandatory/directory analysis. IV. Delegated legislation — conflict with parent Act and rule-making procedure. V. Overlap and distinction with natural justice and discretion review. VI. Remedies and limits of substitution. VII. Conclude that ultra vires restores legality without converting review into appeal.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should written submissions on ultra vires contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Set out the enabling power and the impugned act; identify the precise head of ultra vires; separate jurisdiction from merits; address mandatory procedure if relied on; answer the authority's claim of wide discretion; and seek only the relief supported by the governing law and record.
